É um bom jogo de estratégia, mas um tanto quanto repetitivo.


Guards é um jogo de estratégia em turnos baseado em grade, estruturado em torno de rotação posicional obrigatória de unidades e progressão por campanha. Sua identidade é definida pela gestão de um quarteto fixo de unidades, organizado em três posições frontais e uma retaguarda, sob câmera isométrica fixa que privilegia legibilidade e estabilidade visual.

O núcleo mecânico reside na troca obrigatória de posição entre duas unidades. A rodada só ocorre após a movimentação. A unidade posicionada na retaguarda recupera vida passivamente; ao ser deslocada para a linha de frente, ativa sua habilidade especial. Essa dinâmica transforma o reposicionamento constante no eixo central da estratégia. A tomada de decisão não se limita ao ataque, mas envolve cálculo de exposição e estimativa de dano proveniente das unidades inimigas.

Os inimigos surgem organizados em três faixas alinhadas às posições aliadas, podendo acumular até cinco unidades por faixa. Avançam progressivamente a cada rodada e apresentam características e parâmetros distintos, que escalam conforme o avanço na campanha.

A progressão é cumulativa. A cada mapa finalizado, recursos são concedidos para aprimoramento temporário das unidades; ao final da partida, recursos destinados a aprimoramentos permanentes são obtidos.

A superação das três dificuldades graduais depende do acúmulo progressivo desses recursos, estabelecendo um ciclo de tentativa, coleta, aprimoramento e nova tentativa sob maior exigência. Essa estrutura alonga a duração do jogo, que varia aproximadamente entre quatro e trinta horas, conforme o nível de repetição necessário para a maximização do time escolhido.

A profundidade é moderada: a compreensão inicial é rápida, mas a otimização da rotação e da composição de grupo sustenta a camada estratégica. A expressão do jogador, contudo, permanece limitada ao escopo do quarteto selecionado e às restrições estruturais da campanha linear.

This strategic guard defense game is cleverly tactical and endlessly engaging! 🛡️👮 Outsmart intruders with smart placements 🎮, satisfying puzzles ✨, and escalating challenges. The intuitive mechanics and replay value make it a gem for strategy fans!

Guards by Battlecruiser Games is an inventive yet minimalist take on the turn-based strategy genre, offering a distilled form of tactical play that relies on simplicity rather than sprawling systems. The game places you in charge of a team of four heroes standing against endless waves of enemies, fighting their way toward eventual bosses. At first glance, it appears like many other indie strategy titles—small scale, fantasy-themed, and straightforward—but its defining feature lies in how it transforms traditional combat into something more rhythm-based and positional. Instead of issuing multiple commands or micromanaging units, the player’s only real move is to swap the positions of two characters across the battlefield’s lanes. That small decision, repeated and refined, becomes the beating heart of Guards’ design. Every swap changes the tactical situation, triggering attacks, defenses, and abilities in a delicate dance of timing and placement.

What makes this system interesting is how much strategic nuance emerges from its apparent simplicity. Moving a unit to the front line commits them to attack but also exposes them to danger; pulling them back allows them to rest, heal, or charge up special abilities. Each hero—ranging from melee fighters to ranged specialists and healers—has distinct strengths, and learning how to cycle them efficiently becomes the essence of mastery. This minimalism forces the player to think not in terms of micro-control, but of tempo, flow, and foresight. When it all clicks, the gameplay feels like a carefully orchestrated routine, where each swap is part of a rhythm that keeps your formation alive against increasingly complex enemy patterns. The design encourages both intuition and planning, striking a rare balance between accessibility and thoughtful play that few indie strategy games manage to achieve.

Visually, Guards embraces a straightforward fantasy style that focuses more on clarity than spectacle. The art direction is clean and functional, allowing players to read the battlefield easily, though it rarely surprises or amazes. Environments are limited, often reusing the same backgrounds and monster types, giving the experience a sense of uniformity that some players may find repetitive over time. The characters themselves are familiar archetypes—a witcher, a healer, an archer, a peasant—but their mechanical roles make them distinct enough to feel purposeful. The overall presentation feels more reminiscent of a tabletop skirmish or a board game brought to life than of a grand tactical adventure, and that approach suits its design philosophy. Guards is not about world-building or storytelling; it’s about learning the system and thriving within its constraints.

Progression in Guards unfolds through a steady unlock system that rewards persistence. Players can earn in-game currency to upgrade heroes, purchase new equipment, and recruit stronger allies. This layer of advancement adds incentive to replay levels, but it also reveals the game’s weaker side—the grind. Because the structure revolves around replaying waves of enemies, repetition becomes unavoidable. While unlocking new heroes brings brief bursts of excitement, the underlying gameplay loop remains largely unchanged from start to finish. Without additional mission objectives, branching maps, or varied enemy strategies, the formula can begin to feel static. For those who enjoy fine-tuning small tactical puzzles, the repetition can be meditative and satisfying; for others, it may lead to fatigue long before the game runs its course.

Despite these limitations, Guards carries an understated charm that makes it hard to dismiss. It doesn’t pretend to compete with larger strategy franchises or deliver sweeping narratives; instead, it offers a lean, tightly designed system that rewards short bursts of focus and experimentation. Its quick pacing and easy-to-understand mechanics make it an appealing entry point for players new to the genre, while veterans can appreciate the precision of its tactical rhythm. Each battle is a compact test of resource management, positioning, and timing, and the game’s minimalistic style ensures that every mistake and victory feels earned through player input rather than luck or spectacle. It’s the kind of title that invites return visits not for its story, but for the quiet satisfaction of executing a plan perfectly.

Ultimately, Guards stands as an example of how simplicity can be both a strength and a limitation. Its design philosophy—distilling strategy down to one essential mechanic—creates a refreshing experience that is both approachable and clever, but that same focus also narrows its long-term appeal. The repetition, the modest visuals, and the absence of narrative depth keep it from achieving greatness, yet within its small frame lies a game that knows exactly what it wants to be. For players seeking a quick, clever, and compact strategy experience that values mechanics over complexity, Guards delivers a satisfying and thoughtful diversion. It may not linger in memory as an epic, but its purity of design ensures it stands apart as a rare example of elegance through restraint.

[b]TL;DR:[/b] Guards is a surprisingly fun game that has an easy-to-understand gameplay loop as well as a few challenges for those who seek them.

[b]Guards has a really simple gameplay loop that is easy to understand and fun[/b]. Each turn, you swap the places of two of your heroes, and they perform either special or normal moves depending on how you swap them. When a hero swaps from the first column to the second, they perform a special attack. You aim to create a synergistic team and survive through 10 levels, which consist of monsters with special abilities and a boss at the end.

For a game made in 2016, I'm quite surprised by its quality. [b]The first few hours were really fun, and I finished all the game modes in about 15 hours[/b]. The three different game modes differ in terms of enemy stats and abilities, and they each offer quite a challenge.

[b]One of the not-so-great aspects of Guards is that most of the time, the optimal play is either not important or too blatant[/b]. This is because, as you defeat enemies, you don't know where the next ones will spawn or what their types will be. I'm not saying it would be better that way, but due to this, Guards rely quite a lot on luck at certain encounters, and when it does not, it is quite easy to beat.

The progression in Guards is in three main ways: consumables, hero upgrades, and team upgrades. It is a must to fail in the game a few times to actually be able to beat it, since you need more stats to overcome enemy waves. This results in a lot of grinding to beat the nightmare and hell game modes, as they require a lot of currency to spend to have a chance. So, [b]if you are not a fan of grinding, the game should still last you a few hours before you are bored with it[/b].

[b]Finally, I must say that a couple of achievements are problematic in Guards[/b]. One of them, "TERMINATOR," does not seem to unlock even when you complete its condition, and the "SAGE" achievement seems to be bugged, as the game does not give you enough "stars" to finish it. At least that's what happened with my three end-game saves.

In short, Guards quite surprised me with its quality, and I easily had a few hours of fun with it and even finished the game in all three game modes in over 15 hours. [b]If you don't mind a couple of achievements being stuck, I would suggest you play Guards, as it is quite affordable when it is on discount and provides a few hours of fun at least[/b].

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

+ Interesting core gimmick

- There are 7 possible actions each turn (6 different swaps + inventory), but the interface is not designed around this, so it's easy to choose the wrong action (swapping the wrong heroes) and takes -- what feels like -- wasted effort to do the core gameplay
- after each battle, you get 2-4 random upgrade choices, but won't be able to afford most of them
- help text is unclear or wrong (lvl 2 shield ability says it gives shields per *turn* not per *battle*)

The Ugly
- fastest speed breaks action order, and isn't even all that fast

Verdict
I'm interested in Guards II. Hopefully it will resolve the issues here and make good on the premise

[b]Guards ist ein klassisches Strategiespiel[/b] mit vielen guten Spielelementen. Grafisch auf der Unity–Plattform entwickelte Battlecruiser Games ein anspruchsvolles rundenbasiertes Taktik-Spiel. Grafisch ist Guards gerade noch ausreichend. Der Schwerpunkt liegt offensichtlich im strategischen Segment. Gerne verzichte ich auf grafische Raffinessen, wenn ein Spiel mich ansonsten fordert! Genau das beherrscht Guards sehr gut. Der taktische Teil fordert ungemein, da der Positionswechsel von zwei Protagonisten einen Spielzug darstellt & danach der Gegner am Zug ist. Da sollte jede Handlung wohl überlegt sein, wollen wir im Spiel einige Runden überstehen & Erfolge feiern. 
Zu Beginn stehen uns vier verschiedene Helden zur Verfügung. Je mehr Runden absolviert werden, desto mehr Mithril steht uns zur Verfügung. Mit Mithril lassen sich unsere Helden upgraden & werden so immer Stärker oder erhalten mehr Leben. Zusätzlich lassen sich Aufgaben erledigen, die weiteres Mithril oder Gegenstände freigeben. Mit Mithril lassen sich Gegenstände erwerben, die wir in den Spielrunden einsetzen können. Selbstverständlich können wir in einer Spielrunde nicht unbegrenzt Gegenstände mitführen. Wir müssen genau abwägen, welche Gegenstände uns in den Spielrunden nützlich sein können. Im weiteren Spielverlauf lassen sich vier weitere Helden freischalten. Jeder der acht Helden bringt seine persönlichen Fähigkeiten mit. Hier gilt es eine ausgewogene Balance zu finden, um den Endgegner besiegen zu können.
Guards ist sehr gut in deutscher Sprache übersetzt & eine gelungene Spieleinführung ermöglicht die schnelle Beherrschung der verschiedenen Spielelemente. Gesteuert wird Guards mit der Maus, die Sounds sind einfach & ausreichend. 
Guards überzeugt durch seinen guten taktischen Schwerpunkt, das den Spieler von Runde zu Runde fordert. Liebhaber von rundenbasierten Taktik-Strategiespielen werden ihren Spaß haben. Für den Preis von €4,99 ist Guards ein empfehlenswerter Titel.

Guards - инди-стратегия от отечественного разработчика Battlecruiser Games. Чем игра примечательна и почему в нее стоит сыграть - давайте попробуем разобраться вместе. 

В самом начале нашего игрового пути нам предлагают собрать команду из четверых героев и отправиться на борьбу с местной нечистью. Изначально доступно лишь четыре героя, однако со временем их число увеличивается до 8. Герои на выбор представлены  самых разных типов - рыцари, целители, лучники, ассасины и т.п. В зависимости от типа выбранного героя полностью меняется тактика, которой вам придется руководствоваться в игре. 

Выбрав себе команду, мы попадаем на игровое поле, условно поделенное на квадраты. В одном конце находятся наши воины, в противоположном - наступающие орды противников. Процесс боя поделен на раунды, в течение каждого из которых наши противники делают шаг вперед или же атакуют, если радиус позволяет, в то время как нам достаточно просто выставить троих атакующих героев на переднюю линию, оставив одного "в запасе" на заднем ряду поддержки. Каждый раунд противники обмениваются любезностями - наши герои истребляют орды противников, а условный счетчик вверху экрана показывает, сколько еще нечисти нам осталось перебить до следующего уровня. Каждый ход игрок обязан  изменить положение своих героев на поле боя, отведя самого "раненого" в тыл, где тот получает возможность подлечить раны. По окончанию каждого уровня нам выдают определенную сумму золота и тут же на месте дают его потратить, предлагая  на выбор несколько улучшений для разных типов героев.   

Звучит просто, выглядит еще проще, однако процесс на удивление затягивает и на деле выясняется, что в элементарно выглядящем игровом процессе далеко не все можно пройти с наскока, и придется совершить как минимум несколько рейдов, прежде чем с гордостью получите звание победителя местного мирового зла. 

За каждый совершенный Вами рейд, даже если вам не удалось дойти до главного босса, игроку выдается определенная сумма еще одной местной валюты - мифрила. В перерыве между сражениями можно зайти в магазин и приобрести за мифрил усиливающие героев зелья и руны, а также улучшить характеристики тем игровым персонажам, с которыми собираетесь идти в новый рейд. Одним словом, простор для реиграбельности в наличии имеется. 

В игре есть три уровня сложности, каждый из которых ощутимо отличается от предыдущего и доступен для выбора только по мере последовательного прохождения. Из минусов меня слегка расстроил лишь тот факт, что почему-то не всегда срабатывал "победный скрипт" при одолении главного босса - игра иногда просто зависала, и приходилось проходить по новой. Благо, партии в Guards по времени не такие затянутые, но хотелось бы, чтобы эта проблема решилась разработчиками. 

Помню, когда вышла Disciples III, в которой отечественные разработчики во всем, в чем только можно ушли от изначальных корней серии, фанаты предыдущих частей возопили "Верните нам позиционные сражения! Не дадим превратить Disciples в Героев Меча и Магии". Собственно, именно эти поиски игры со статичным положением юнитов на поле боя и привели меня к Guards. У игры приемлемая цена и по итогу я готов её порекомендовать всем, кого не пугают инди-стратегии.
